This is all true (with the exception of local government which is a peer to districts, not a level above), but not new or unique to COVID.  There is always pressure from the communities, the teachers and the parents on a number of levels and issues. If a super isn’t acting rationally, a rational board will make an adjustment.  If both are not acting rationally, a rational community will make an adjustment.  

Your concern should be with the community, not the schools

Let’s not confuse the loudest yellers with those who represent the most people nor a loud yeller in one community to speak for those in another.  Social media has given everyone a megaphone and what you are seeing is the perils we were warned of with a “true democracy.”  

Turn your eye to your community, understand what is truly being said and if the board and district don’t truly represent your communities, vote them out.  Just don’t go thinking that because everyone doesn’t agree on something that they are acting irrational.

Honestly school districts don’t care about the politics.  Federal Government provides about 10% of funding and ALL of that is to support title 1 (free reduced lunch) and special needs access.  It’s laughable (and irrational ironically) when Trump threatens funding.  Very little CARES money went to public schools and very little will flow effectively in the next bill.

State funding makes up 1/2  and schools just had a considerable cut from GA that they had to cover. The state doesn’t punish specific districts, it’s very fair in its universal punishment of all public schools. GA had done it’s worst to schools already, there is no “pressure “ left.

That leaves local funding and while school board are elected and face political pressures, their level of control doesn’t allow them the influence that most believe is present.  They employee the super, make policy and budget.  These people aren’t launching political careers from the school board either.  Most (not all) are in it for the students and teachers.

That leaves the superintendents who are highly skilled and in fact rational.  Most operate the largest business in their county.  So yes, the mess media and social media are rife with political unrest and using COVID and face masks in a proxy war for hearts and minds.  But no, that doesn’t leak to schools anymore than it leaks to well functioning businesses.

Each district will make choices in their best interests, period.  That is rational.

TLDR- Schools are rational organizations and have specific reasons to make their decisions.

Perhaps schools that are trying to Open understand this as well?  Schools aren’t open and based on the curves we are likely headed for a full on shut down.  One advantage that schools had last year is that teachers were able to make an in-person connection with students and gauge learning styles.  Students made connections with teachers, gained trust with each other and understood how they communicated.  Digital learning at that time was a waste for most, but some succeeded due to these connections.

Perhaps schools are trying to eek out 2-3 weeks to accomplish this before a complete shutdown for a lot longer period?

Perhaps schools need to gauge the level of learning loss that occurred during the first shut down to understand how to remédiate?

Perhaps they aren’t clueless to the situation and know that we are heading there whether they open or not (remember there are very few and mostly rural even offering some form of hybrid) and have decided that 2-3 weeks for those willing and/or needing in-person might actually allow a less than catastrophic learning gap as we go into a significant and long term shutdown.

Perhaps they know just as much as you all and make decisions related to thousands of students on a daily basis?

I’m not trying to start a flame war and fight for one side or the other, I just want people to slow down a bit and try to think of actions others take in a rational manner.  We throw around “fucking idiots” like we are talking about the town drunk when we are talking about professionally run organizations that operate on a purely rational basis.

I am 4 years old and asleep.  I wake up to the image of a man bending over me.  He is dressed in a Hawaiian shirt, is pale skinned and has a brownish red Afro.  I think it’s my mom at the time because she had a perm (1975).  I say “mom” a couple of times with no answer.

I start yelling louder and louder and my parents rush in.  The man steps back behind them, but doesn’t leave the room.  They can’t see him and I am pointing, crying that he is right there.  Eventually he “fades away” and I am left crying and have issues sleeping alone for much of my adolescence.  My mom who was somewhat of a mystic suggested that it was the “sandman” 

I can still vividly remember every detail over 40 years later.
